The poem named after this figure was written by Eugamon of Cyrene, and one alternate ending to that poem sees him fathering of Italus, who founded Italy. In the first book of that work, this character's father receives a beautiful mixing bowl from Polyxenius and fathers Polypoites with Callidice after he becomes king of the Thesprotians. In the second book of that work, this character mistakes a certain island for Corcyra and kills his dad inadvertently with a staff that has a sting ray attached. Shortly afterwards, this man's half-brother marries Circe, and this man marries Penelope. For 15 points, identify this figure, the son of Circe and Odysseus.
